discovery: Photonic crystals: the photonic band gap and control of light emission and confinement in periodic dielectric structures
motivation: In 1987 Yablonovitch and John independently showed that a periodic dielectric can forbid photon propagation over a band of frequencies. Yablonovitch proposed it to suppress spontaneous emission; John proposed it to localize light. Yablonovitch then gave the first experimental demonstration of a full three-dimensional photonic band gap. Noda turned the concept into real optical-frequency devices: three-dimensional band-gap crystals, ultrahigh-Q nanocavities, and photonic-crystal surface-emitting lasers that are now being commercialized. Together they created a new way to engineer the electromagnetic vacuum itself. Photonic crystals made possible cavity quantum electrodynamics with single solid-state emitters, Purcell-enhanced single-photon sources, low-threshold nanolasers, photonic-crystal fibres, slow light and topological photonics. Today they are core building blocks of integrated classical and quantum photonics. Few concepts in optics have been as fundamental and as widely used.
